name: Neu!
hook: Two musicians who left Kraftwerk in 1971 and made the steady, forward-driving beat that rock would call motorik.
blurb: Michael Rother and Klaus Dinger both played in Kraftwerk in 1971, then left and started Neu! in Düsseldorf. Dinger's drumming was a steady beat that never changes and never stops. Critics named it motorik, though Dinger preferred his own name for it, the Apache beat. Rother layered guitars over it. They made three albums between 1972 and 1975 with the producer Conny Plank; the end year here is 1975, the last of those three. They sold modestly at the time, and the influence came later, through David Bowie's Berlin records and then through post-punk and indie bands for decades. Bowie was a fan and named his song 'Heroes' after their track 'Hero'. The records are guitar and drums, but the band sits in the electronic lineage on this map because of their place in the Düsseldorf scene next to Kraftwerk.

signatureTracks.title: Hallogallo
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Ten minutes of one beat, the first statement of motorik.

signatureTracks.title: Hero
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Dinger's shouted vocal over the same beat, faster and angrier. The song Bowie's 'Heroes' is named after.
